catalog_quote: [Boyce 1954: 47-48] A study of stress is attended by some difficulties, for the position of stress in Middle Iranian is not yet certain. Henning has adopted as a working hypothesis the principle of stress upon the final syllable within the word, which accords with later Western Iranian practice. The question of which words are to be stressed is often [p. 48] simplified by the fact that a poem with, apparently, three stresses to a line will contain many lines with only three words, or with three words and a conjunction or preposition. In such cases it is simple to assign the stress. Both the Parthian hymn-cycles appear to have four stresses to a line ... [Henning 1942: 52] All Middle Iranian poetry, Middle Persian, Parthian, and Khotanese, has this feature in common that the number of syllables to a line is variable. The important point throughout is the number of stressed syllables. ...…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is assumed to fall on the last syllable of the word (Henning's working hypothesis, adopted by Boyce for scanning the Manichaean Parthian hymn-cycles); the position of stress in Middle Iranian is explicitly said to be not yet established. Lines carry four stresses, one per lexical word; conjunctions and prepositions are unstressed; the number of unstressed syllables between stresses varies.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; a few half-lines with only one stressable word lead Boyce to infer either two main stresses on one word or three-stress lines (p. 50).
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress position; uncertainty is about which words bear stress (function words unstressed). The source itself flags the whole placement as uncertain.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress as used in metrical scansion of Manichaean Parthian verse (Angad Rosnan, Huwidagman, Turfan manuscripts); not a phonological description in a grammar. Tertiary sources give the same final-stress rule for the sister language Middle Persian (Sundermann 1989: 145; Rastorgueva 1966: 29; Skjaervo 2009: 202).
new_statements.identity_note: The statement concerns Manichaean (literary) Parthian of the Turfan texts (hymn-cycles Angad Rosnan and Huwidagman, 3rd-4th c. compositions in later copies); Glottolog has no subdivision of part1239, so the language-level code applies. Boyce phrases it as 'Middle Iranian' generally, with Parthian as the object of study.

sources.quote: A study of stress is attended by some difficulties, for the position of stress in Middle Iranian is not yet certain. Henning has adopted as a working hypothesis the principle of stress upon the final syllable within the word, which accords with later Western Iranian practice. The question of which words are to be stressed is often simplified by the fact that a poem with, apparently, three stresses to a line will contain many lines with only three words, or with three words and a conjunction or preposition.
sources.note: p. 47: position of stress in Middle Iranian 'not yet certain'; adopts Henning's working hypothesis of stress on the final syllable of the word (as in later Western Iranian) and scans the Parthian hymn-cycles with four stresses per line on that basis; unstressed syllables vary in number; function words (conjunctions, prepositions) unstressed.
